svg.text: The article runs as one long chain: each proposed mechanism answers a problem raised by the one before it,
climbing from connectionism's failure up to a wave-based theory of consciousness, with the comparison to rival
theories sitting as a side note just before the conclusion.

g.text: From fixed neurons to conscious waves
A chain of steps, each one driven by a gap the previous step left open; two crowded steps are expanded in the zooms
below, and a comparison to rival theories hangs off to the side near the end.

g.title: Cognition needs rapid coordination — of millions of neurons, fast — Flexible top-down thought requires coordinating hundreds of millions of neurons within fractions of a second. — → spya-f6m6jv

Classical view: each neuron has one fixed job — but this can't explain the data — Hierarchical feedforward models assign each neuron a stable specialized function, but about a third of all prefrontal neurons engage in any given task. — → spya-k046f6
g.text: Classical view: each neuron has one fixed
but this can't explain the data

g.title: Many neurons multiplex signals (mixed selectivity) — A neuron may respond to an object only in one sequence position, blending identity, order, and action in one cell. — → spya-v0gbwq

Brain waves can shift spiking directly — ephaptic coupling, no synapse needed — Oscillating electric fields modulate nearby neurons' spiking directly, independent of synaptic connections. — → spya-jnp59d
g.text: Brain waves can shift spiking directly

g.title: Spatial Computing: alpha/beta 'stencils' gate gamma spiking — Spatially patterned alpha/beta rhythms suppress gamma-driven spiking in some cortical spots while sparing others, routing information. — → spya-qck2sw

This explains mixed selectivity and low-dimensional coding — A neuron falls inside or outside the suppressive stencil depending on context, producing context-dependent tuning without dedicated 'context neurons'. — → spya-zmknun

Traveling waves shift activity between coding states — Moving patterns of excitation and inhibition sweep across cortex and may move population activity between orthogonal coding subspaces. — → spya-y09vju
Wave interference performs analog computation — efficient, all at once — Overlapping waves add, cancel, and combine continuously, computing in parallel rather than one step at a time. — → spya-h5qjz4

Anesthesia disrupts waves, not specific receptors — Very different drugs all converge on the same outcome: slow, desynchronized cortical waves, suggesting consciousness tracks wave organization. — → spya-uvev07

Hybrid framework: synapses store, waves control the moment — Synaptic wiring stores long-term knowledge; wave patterns, via ephaptic feedback and analog computation, decide which representations are active right now. — → spya-dnv2tp

Compared with Global Workspace, IIT, Higher-Order theories — Shares themes with these theories but locates the mechanism in wave-based organization rather than broadcasting, a 'hot zone', or a separate observer. — → spya-xn7mdj

Consciousness: an organized, wave-coordinated cortex — Consciousness emerges when wave patterns bring the cortex into a unified, globally integrated state, built on ordinary cortical physics. — → spya-smkrcs

g.text: Why mixed selectivity needs a router
A funnel: the failure of fixed-function neurons, the discovery of multifunctional ones, and the resulting need for a
routing system, narrowing down onto oscillations and ephaptic coupling as the answer.

g.title: A given task engages ~1/3 of all PFC neurons — Under a fixed-function view, the brain would saturate after learning just three tasks, so neurons must be multifunctional instead. — → spya-amx5qf
g.text: A given task engages ~1/3 of all PFC neurons

g.title: Neurons encode nonlinear combinations of variables — This is called mixed selectivity: neurons blend sensory, motor, and contextual information rather than representing one thing. — → spya-v0gbwq
E.g. a neuron fires to object A only if seen first — The same neuron fires to object B only if it comes second, showing context-dependent, not fixed, tuning. — → spya-x5m34h
g.text: E.g. a neuron fires to object A only if seen

g.title: This hugely expands storage and computing power — Multiplexing information across many flexible neurons stores far more than segregating it into narrow specialists. — → spya-njs6ff
g.text: This hugely expands storage and computing

g.title: Cortex is overlapping networks, not fixed modules — The same neurons can take part in different computations at different times, shifting network membership as needed. — → spya-fnm872
g.text: Cortex is overlapping networks, not fixed

g.title: Problem: how to route signals without knowing which synapses to use — Dynamically routing signals through a dense web of overlapping networks is hard to reconcile with a purely synaptic-weight framework. — → spya-dtnkkk
g.text: Problem: how to route signals without knowing

g.title: Candidate answer: neural oscillations — organize, route, time spiking — Oscillations segregate spiking into phases, route information locally, and open timing windows for long-range communication. — → spya-jnp59d

Ephaptic coupling: fields shift spiking without synapses — Extracellular electric fields can directly nudge nearby neurons' membrane potential, synchronizing them even when synapses are blocked. — → spya-mapqhv

Fields spread wider, act continuously, near-instantly — Unlike sparse, brief spikes limited by axon conduction, fields cover millimeters at once and change almost at the speed of light. — → spya-j7k4hu

So oscillatory fields suit rapid, large-scale control — These properties make brain waves good candidates for aligning spike timing and flexibly routing information across overlapping networks. — → spya-f59f0p
g.text: So oscillatory fields suit rapid, large-scale
Spatial Computing, traveling waves, analog computation
A chain within a chain: the stencil mechanism is proposed, confirmed, and shown to explain two puzzles, then extended
in time (traveling waves) and generalized into a computing principle (wave interference).

g.title: Gamma excites; alpha/beta brakes, like in motor cortex — Beta acts as a brake on movement; when it drops locally, gamma and spiking rise and movement becomes likely. — → spya-thnz7b
g.text: Gamma excites; alpha/beta brakes, like in

g.title: Alpha/beta act as inhibitory 'stencils' over cortex — Alpha/beta rhythms suppress gamma and spiking in targeted spots, letting feedforward signals emerge only where alpha/beta is weak. — → spya-gkfdys
Confirmed in monkey PFC: patterns predict errors — Alpha/beta rhythms carried learned contextual information in spatial patterns that mirrored sensory spiking and predicted mistakes. — → spya-azz3c8
g.text: Confirmed in monkey PFC: patterns predict

g.title: Alpha/beta's millimeter scale suits top-down control — Wave spatial reach tracks frequency: gamma is too fine-grained, slow waves too broad; alpha/beta sits at just the right scale. — → spya-q606tk

This explains mixed selectivity, no 'context neuron' needed — A neuron falls inside the stencil in one context and outside it in another, making its apparent selectivity context-dependent. — → spya-zmknun

And explains low-dimensional 'subspace' coding — Stencils segregate spiking into overlapping, structured subsets of neurons, which looks like organizing activity into separate subspaces. — → spya-xphb7u
Traveling waves move the stencil across cortex — Alpha/beta patterns do not just sit still; they sweep across the cortical surface as organized traveling waves. — → spya-y09vju
g.text: Traveling waves move the stencil across

g.title: Moving stencils may drive shifts between coding states — As a wave moves, it can transition population activity from one orthogonal coding subspace to another. — → spya-mrsvfu
g.text: Moving stencils may drive shifts between

g.title: Wave interference performs analog computation directly — When waves meet they add, cancel, or form new patterns through superposition, solving problems the way physical wave physics works. — → spya-vp5h33

This is parallel and far more energy-efficient — than step-by-step digital computing — An analog medium evolves all at once rather than looping through variables one at a time, which also saves energy. — → spya-mgnqxk
g.text: This is parallel and far more
